clue.text: Music from the Ivories for diners out east

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a simple waltz every beginner bangs out on the piano, whose keys are the ivories
second meaning: the pair of sticks people in East Asia eat with

explanation.surface: A dinner in a Far Eastern restaurant, with someone at the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The ivories are piano keys. The tune and the eating sticks share one name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a famous elementary piano piece and the pair of eating implements used across China and Japan.

clue.text: Bay of bounds perhaps

parts.note: surface reading: a reddish-brown horse, the kind that bounds over fences
setter's reading: a great inlet whose shores form the boundary of several Canadian provinces, named after an English explorer

explanation.walkthrough: Bay is a capital-B place name, not a horse: Hudson Bay in northern Canada is bounded by Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec and Nunavut. The 1978 newspaper scan may have garbled a letter in this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hudson Bay, named after the explorer Henry Hudson, is the vast inland sea whose coast marks the borders of several Canadian territories.

clue.text: Not all Shaw's plays were so nice

definitions.text: Not all Shaw's plays were so nice

parts.words: Not all Shaw's plays were so nice
parts.note: surface reading: a theatregoer's grumble that some of Shaw's plays were unkind
setter's reading: Shaw sorted his early plays into two published volumes, one with this agreeable word in its title and one with its opposite

explanation.surface: A critic remarks that some of Bernard Shaw's plays were less than kind.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw grouped his early plays as Plays Pleasant and Plays Unpleasant, so literally not all of them were the nice kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and agreeable are synonyms, and the word is the label Shaw gave one group of his early dramas.

clue.text: Forger's device to foul an E London footballer

parts.note: to trip someone is to foul them in football
West Ham United, an East London football club, are nicknamed the Hammers

explanation.surface: A footballer from East London commits a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The forger here works metal at a forge, not a counterfeiter of banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip hammer is a heavy power-driven hammer raised and dropped by a cam, used by smiths at a forge.

clue.text: Guilty one put right 151 misapplied

indicators.note: something misapplied is put to the wrong use, so these letters are set down in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
151 in Roman numerals: C for 100, L for 50, I for 1

explanation.surface: Someone guilty is told to fix a misused figure of 151.
explanation.definitionFit: The person responsible for a crime or fault is the guilty party, the offender.

clue.text: Presume not God to - (Pope)

parts.note: surface reading: a quotation with its last word blanked out
setter's reading: Alexander Pope's Essay on Man opens a couplet with 'Know then thyself, presume not God to' and a verb meaning examine closely

explanation.walkthrough: The poet, not the pontiff: Alexander Pope wrote 'Know then thyself, presume not God to scan; The proper study of mankind is man.'
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means scrutinise or examine closely, which Pope says humans should not presume to do to the divine.

clue.text: Obtained for discharged patients?

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
patients are discharged from hospital once healed

explanation.surface: A query about what was got for patients leaving hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to acquire or get hold of it, so obtained is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Litter etc-replace In orderly fashion here

definitions.text: Litter etc-replace In orderly fashion here

indicators.note: putting things in orderly fashion means arranging them, so the jumbled letters are tidied into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded sign telling people to put their litter back neatly here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a sign on a litter bin asking you to put your rubbish in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is a container, such as the bin that rubbish is put into to keep a place tidy.

clue.text: Not a whole meal of this, naturally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one dish of a meal, such as the soup or the pudding

definitions.note: the phrase of course means naturally
definitions.meaning: second meaning: put the word after of and the phrase means naturally

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a fill-in: of ___ means naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter or dessert is one part of a meal, and the phrase of course is an everyday synonym for naturally or certainly.

clue.text: Slight advantage to Sir Rowland- land in battle

parts.note: a slight lead over a rival is an edge
Sir Rowland Hill was the Victorian reformer who introduced the penny post

explanation.surface: Sir Rowland gains a slight advantage on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill, a ridge in Warwickshire, was the site of the first big battle of the English Civil War in 1642.
explanation.definitionFit: The ridge in Warwickshire is a stretch of high ground famous as the field of the first Civil War battle.

clue.text: Magic figure of ten perhaps in a different place

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
perhaps marks a word as only one possible version, so its letters may be shuffled
a different arrangement of a word means its letters are reordered

parts.note: the three letters of ten reordered
the letters of place reordered, with the first piece set inside after the P

explanation.surface: A magic figure involving the number ten turns up somewhere unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentacle is a five-pointed star or similar symbol used in magic and occult ritual.

clue.text: I played opposite the king

parts.note: surface reading: an actor boasting about a leading role
setter's reading: the I of the musical The King and I, the English governess at the Siamese court

explanation.walkthrough: In The King and I, the I is the governess Anna Leonowens, the role opposite King Mongkut of Siam.
explanation.definitionFit: The governess's name is the I in the musical's title, the character who acts opposite the King of Siam.

clue.text: But it's more likely to get the wind up than its owner

definitions.text: But it's more likely to get the wind up than its owner

parts.note: surface reading: to become frightened, and something frightening sounds an alarm
setter's reading: the device has its spring wound each night by the person who keeps it by the bed

explanation.walkthrough: Get the wind up means take fright, but a clockwork bedside timepiece literally gets wound up every evening, more often than its owner panics.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside timepiece with a bell, wound nightly, rings at a set hour to wake the sleeper.

clue.text: The best in his class

parts.note: surface reading: a top pupil at school
setter's reading: social class, the Greek root aristos meaning best

explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Greek aristos, best, plus rule; class is social rank, not a schoolroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble belongs to the highest social rank, and the Greek root of the word literally means rule by the best.

clue.text: With which to survey the old bishop with the odd tile

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters are rearranged into an unusual sequence

parts.note: taken as written
Odo, Bishop of Bayeux, was William the Conqueror's half-brother in the eleventh century
the four letters of tile reordered

explanation.surface: A surveyor's kit described as an ancient bishop and a misfitting tile.
explanation.walkthrough: Old here means long ago: Bishop Odo of Bayeux appears in the Bayeux Tapestry.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is the tripod-mounted instrument surveyors use to measure horizontal and vertical angles across land.

clue.text: A refusal to include Brown for science

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
Tom Brown is the hero of the Victorian novel Tom Brown's Schooldays

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let Brown join a science class.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown looks like a colour; it is the surname of Tom Brown, so it gives his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the branch of biology that studies the structure of bodies, a science taught in medical schools.

clue.text: Hard to fathom a trick about our Summer Time

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
BST is British Summer Time, ours to a London newspaper

explanation.surface: Daylight saving is a confusing trick played on us.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's newspaper was British, so our Summer Time is British Summer Time, the clocks put forward an hour each spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abstruse is obscure and difficult to understand, which is what hard to fathom says.

clue.text: "" Airy " description of Broadway film?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: full of airs, tunes
second meaning: the adjective from the 1929 musical The Broadway Melody

explanation.walkthrough: Airy is read as full of airs, tunes, rather than light or breezy. The Broadway Melody was an early Hollywood musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, so something tuneful is airy in that sense, and the adjective describes a film named Melody.

clue.text: Theatre performer gets a number for you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a surgeon working in the operating theatre
second meaning: the switchboard worker who connects telephone calls

explanation.walkthrough: Theatre is the operating theatre, not the stage, and the number is a telephone number, not a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations in a hospital theatre, and a telephone exchange worker puts calls through to the number requested.

clue.text: Understand about ship, how one may go off course

parts.note: dig is slang for understand or appreciate
re means about or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor grasps how a ship can stray from its route.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject in speech or writing, a figurative straying from the planned route.

clue.text: BBC's brainchild ?

parts.note: surface reading: an idea someone invented
setter's reading: the BBC television quiz with the famous black chair, whose whole subject is brains

explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running BBC television quiz, first shown in 1972, where contestants answer on a specialist subject from a black chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiz programme was created by the British broadcaster, and the word also means a person of great intellect, a brainy creation.

clue.text: Weight thrown in middle of deep river

indicators.note: something thrown in is tossed inside, so one piece sits within another
the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two at the centre

parts.note: the two letters at the centre of deep
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A heavy object is tossed into the deepest part of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elbe is a major central European river flowing from the Czech Republic through Germany to the North Sea.

clue.text: Joy not unalloyed, winning this medal?

parts.note: surface reading: mixed feelings, happiness that is not pure
surface padding: the winner of the award, carrying the scene of a sports podium
setter's reading: the third-place medal is made of an alloy of copper and tin, so its winner's joy is alloyed in both senses

explanation.walkthrough: Unalloyed means pure. Third place is a mixed pleasure, and its medal is itself a copper-tin alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: The third-place award in sport is made of a copper and tin alloy, matching the not unalloyed joke.

clue.text: Birds imitate a cat, we hear, in the flower-bed

definitions.note: names the plant by where it grows

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: we hear marks a word chosen by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a cat makes a contented rumbling noise

explanation.surface: Birds in a garden sound like a contented cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a tall garden plant with spikes of blue or purple blooms, often grown in borders.

clue.text: Particoloured French supporter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: patched in two or more colours
second meaning: the French for foot, which a body stands on

explanation.walkthrough: A foot supports the body, so a French supporter is the French word for foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pied means patched in different colours, as of a magpie, and in French it is the word for a foot.

clue.text: Being a way-out gun-carrier

definitions.note: an adjective here, as in now being

indicators.note: a carrier holds its load inside, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: an exit is a way out
the Sten was a British sub-machine gun of the Second World War

explanation.surface: Something eccentric that carries a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Way-out looks like the slang for eccentric, but it is the door you leave by.
explanation.definitionFit: Existent means having actual existence, currently in being, which is the adjective sense of being.

clue.text: Helmet said to hold liquor

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is chosen by its sound

parts.note: a barrel used to store wine or spirits

explanation.surface: A soldier's helmet is used as a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A casque is an old word for a piece of armour worn on the head, from French.

clue.text: Do this and there is somehow a loss of spirit

definitions.text: Do this and there is somehow a loss of spirit

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together by some unspecified method, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that doing this will leave someone deflated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: to cause a loss of spirit is to make someone downhearted.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten someone is to discourage them and sap their courage and enthusiasm.
